options: thiamine (vitamin B1) in the outer layers

questions.stem: A pan of oil catches fire on the cooker. The safest action is to

questions.stem: Food handlers should wash their hands

questions.stem: A sign of freshness in fish is

bright, bulging eyes and red gills

questions.stem: Which of the following is a cereal?
questions.explanation: Sorghum is a cereal grain; cowpea and groundnut are legumes.

questions.explanation: Cassava contains cyanogenic glycosides that release hydrogen cyanide.

questions.stem: Which of these is a dry heat method of cooking?

questions.explanation: Heat denatures and sets (coagulates) protein.

questions.stem: Food placed under a hot grill is cooked mainly by

eggs and sugar are whisked to trap air and no fat is used

half as much fat as flour

heat adds air to the dough

questions.explanation: Yeast ferments sugar to carbon dioxide and alcohol.

options: is usually cheaper per unit and saves shopping time

questions.explanation: Fast-food outlets prepare and sell food.

options: Using expired ingredients to save cost

questions.stem:
(a) State three functions of protein in the body. [3 marks]
(b) Name two animal and two plant sources of protein. [4 marks]
(c) Name one protein deficiency disease and state three of its symptoms. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Any three (1 each): growth; repair of worn-out tissues; formation of enzymes and hormones; formation of antibodies; supply of energy
2 marks: Animal sources (any two): meat, fish, eggs, milk, poultry
2 marks: Plant sources (any two): beans, soya bean, groundnut, melon, cowpea
1 mark: Kwashiorkor (accept marasmus)
2 marks: Any symptoms (award up to 2): oedema/swelling; pot belly; changes in hair colour; skin lesions; poor growth; apathy
questions.explanation: Protein builds and repairs tissues and forms enzymes, hormones and antibodies. Animal: meat, fish, eggs; plant: beans, soya. Kwashiorkor shows oedema, pot belly, discoloured hair and poor growth.

questions.stem:
(a) What is meal planning? [2 marks]
(b) State eight factors to consider when planning meals for a family. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Meal planning: deciding in advance the foods/dishes to be served at meals to meet the needs of the family
8 marks: Any eight (1 each): nutritional needs; age of family members; occupation/activity level; health conditions; family income/budget; season and availability of food; time available; equipment available; religion/customs; likes and dislikes; variety of colour, flavour and texture; skill of the cook
questions.explanation: Meal planning decides in advance what to serve. Factors: nutritional needs, age, occupation, health, income, season, time, equipment, religion, preferences and variety.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain what diabetes mellitus is. [2 marks]
(b) State four dietary guidelines for a diabetic person. [4 marks]
(c) Plan a one-day menu (breakfast, lunch and dinner) suitable for a diabetic adult. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: A condition in which the body cannot properly control blood glucose because of insufficient insulin or poor response to insulin
4 marks: Any four (1 each): limit sugar and sugary drinks; regular meals at fixed times; choose high-fibre whole grains, beans and vegetables; control portion sizes; reduce fat; avoid alcohol; maintain healthy weight
4 marks: Suitable menu with low sugar, adequate fibre and lean protein for all three meals, e.g. unsweetened oat pap with boiled egg; brown rice with vegetable stew and fish; beans porridge with vegetables
questions.explanation: Diabetes is poor blood glucose control due to insulin problems. Diet: little sugar, high fibre, regular meals, controlled portions, low fat. Menu example: oats and egg; brown rice, vegetable stew, fish; beans and vegetables.

questions.stem:
(a) State five personal hygiene practices a food handler should observe. [5 marks]
(b) State five ways of preventing food-borne diseases in the home. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
5 marks: Any five (1 each): wash hands before handling food and after toilet; keep nails short and clean; cover hair; wear clean apron; do not cough or sneeze over food; cover cuts with waterproof dressing; avoid handling food when ill; avoid smoking/spitting in the kitchen
5 marks: Any five (1 each): cook food thoroughly; store food at correct temperatures; cover food from flies; use clean, safe water; wash fruits and vegetables; separate raw and cooked foods; keep kitchen clean and control pests; reheat leftovers thoroughly
questions.explanation: Food handlers should wash hands, keep nails short, cover hair and cuts, and stay away when ill. Prevent food-borne illness by thorough cooking, cold storage, covering food, clean water and separating raw from cooked food.

questions.stem:
(a) Name four parts of an egg. [4 marks]
(b) Describe two ways of testing an egg for freshness. [4 marks]
(c) State two uses of eggs in cookery. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: Any four (1 each): shell; shell membranes; air cell/space; albumen (white); yolk; chalazae
2 marks: Salt water test: fresh egg sinks and lies flat; stale egg floats
2 marks: Breaking test: fresh egg has a firm, rounded yolk and thick white; stale egg has a flat yolk and watery white (accept candling/shake test)
2 marks: Any two (1 each): binding; coating; glazing; emulsifying; raising/aerating; thickening; garnishing; enriching
questions.explanation: Egg parts: shell, membranes, air cell, white, yolk, chalazae. Freshness: sinks in salt water; firm yolk and thick white when broken. Uses: binding, coating, glazing, aerating, emulsifying.

questions.stem:
(a) State two principles underlying food preservation. [2 marks]
(b) Describe four methods of preserving food, giving one example of a food preserved by each. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Any two (1 each): destroy or inactivate microorganisms and enzymes; remove conditions for microbial growth (moisture, warmth); prevent recontamination
8 marks: Any four methods described with example (2 each): drying - fish, pepper, okra; smoking - fish, meat; salting - fish, meat; freezing/refrigeration - meat, fish; canning/bottling - tomatoes, fruits; sugaring - jam; pickling - onions, cucumbers; fermentation - ogi
questions.explanation: Preservation destroys or inactivates microbes and enzymes and prevents recontamination. Methods: drying (fish), smoking (fish), salting, freezing (meat), canning (tomatoes), sugaring (jam), pickling (vegetables).

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between moist heat and dry heat methods of cooking, giving two examples of each. [6 marks]
(b) State the effect of heat on (i) protein; (ii) starch in moist heat. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Moist heat: food cooked in water, liquid or steam
1 mark: Moist examples (any two): boiling, stewing, steaming, poaching, braising
2 marks: Dry heat: food cooked by hot air, radiant heat or hot fat
1 mark: Dry examples (any two): baking, roasting, grilling, frying, toasting
2 marks: Protein coagulates/sets and hardens; overheating makes it tough and less digestible
2 marks: Starch granules absorb water, swell and burst (gelatinise), thickening the liquid and becoming more digestible
questions.explanation: Moist heat uses water or steam (boiling, steaming); dry heat uses air, radiation or fat (baking, grilling, frying). Heat coagulates protein and gelatinises starch in liquid.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the three raising agents used in flour mixtures and state how each is introduced. [6 marks]
(b) State four rules for making a successful cake by the creaming method. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Air: by sieving flour, creaming fat and sugar, whisking eggs, rubbing-in, folding
2 marks: Steam: from liquid in the mixture in a hot oven (batters, choux pastry)
2 marks: Carbon dioxide: from baking powder, bicarbonate of soda with acid, or yeast
4 marks: Any four (1 each): measure ingredients accurately; cream fat and sugar until light and fluffy; add eggs gradually to prevent curdling; fold in flour lightly; preheat oven to correct temperature; do not open oven door early; grease and line tins
questions.explanation: Raising agents: air (sieving, creaming, whisking), steam (liquid in hot oven), CO2 (baking powder, yeast). Creaming: accurate weighing, cream well, add egg gradually, fold flour lightly, preheated oven.

questions.stem:
(a) State four conditions necessary for yeast to grow. [4 marks]
(b) Outline the main steps in making bread rolls. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: Food (sugar), warmth (about 25-30 °C), moisture, time (accept: correct salt level, no excessive heat)
6 marks: Steps (1 each): activate yeast in lukewarm liquid with sugar; mix with flour and salt to a dough; knead until smooth and elastic; leave to rise/prove in a warm place; knock back and shape into rolls, prove again; bake in a hot oven until brown and hollow-sounding
questions.explanation: Yeast needs food, warmth, moisture and time. Bread rolls: activate yeast, mix dough, knead, prove, shape, prove again, bake in a hot oven.

questions.stem:
(a) What is a "cover" in table setting? [2 marks]
(b) Describe how a cover is laid for a three-course lunch of soup, main course and dessert. [5 marks]
(c) State three rules of table etiquette. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: The space and set of cutlery, crockery and glassware laid for one person
5 marks: Correct cover (award up to 5): dinner plate position centre; soup spoon outermost on right; main knife on right blade inwards; main fork on left; dessert spoon and fork above the plate; glass at tip of the knife; side plate on left with napkin
3 marks: Any three (1 each): chew with mouth closed; do not talk with food in mouth; wait for others/host before starting; use cutlery properly; do not reach across others; place cutlery together on plate when finished
questions.explanation: A cover is the place setting for one person. For soup, main and dessert: soup spoon outermost right, knife right, fork left, dessert cutlery above the plate, glass above the knife, side plate left. Etiquette: close mouth when chewing, wait for others, do not reach across.
